sections.heading: Planning your Dorset Gardens interior
sections.text:
District 8 is an inner-city, fine-grain neighbourhood: older streets, a mix of housing, and a very different atmosphere from a new-town EC. Owners who buy here often want the new apartment to feel calm once the door is closed — proper storage, a living room that is not a dump of loose cabinets, and bedrooms that are fully fitted — while still being practical about shoes, bags and weekday cooking. That is a joinery brief. Maison would start, once an approved plan exists, with an entry cabinet, a living-room storage wall, a fitted kitchen with a tall pantry, and full-height wardrobes. We specify built-in carpentry, not IKEA-style furniture, and we can work in close, material-led photographs as well as a wide room view.

No official floor plan is on file, so typologies and room sizes are not listed, and we will not invent a typical Dorset Gardens layout. Orchard Sophia and the District 9 pages sit just to the west; Kent Heights and Towner Residences, already live, sit in the wider Kallang and Farrer Park catchment. Those are nearby links. We will not invent walking times to Farrer Park MRT or to Little India. Check your eventual stack, facing and the management rules before you plan blinds or a window bench, especially if the road is busy.

It is early for on-site work if the launch itself is still planned. When a plan and a purchase timeline are in your hands, WhatsApp Maison and we can start from those documents. After keys, the sequence is defects, measurement, renovation approval, then fabrication. A moderate carpentry scope is often planned at six to ten weeks on site after approvals, as an editorial figure only. We are not affiliated with the developers.
